commits.message: Remove an import the deleted committee store test left unused

Drop three test expectations that named deleted code

The SDK layer owners list still named the deleted cek-selection module, the committee store test still expected the removed store upgrade to refill a missing commit clock, and the Flat encoder differential test asserted a program count that included the deleted script-decode-step fixtures.

Drop duration and lint-baseline entries for deleted files

The three CI duration tables still listed test files this branch deletes, and the lint baseline kept one site in a deleted export. Neither affects coverage; they are removed so the tables describe files that exist.

Remove the watcher's legacy journal directory warnings

Prelaunch deployments start with a fresh journal, so no watcher will find a leftover file journal or an old proof layout to warn about. The startup checks, their module, their test and the README section describing them are removed.

Remove the committee store upgrade

Launch starts every committee from a fresh store, so the in-place upgrade of older stores never runs. It covered the conflict-evidence column drop, the end-time backfill, the outbox quarantine-field strip and the L1 record upgrade. The block_time_ms column that the upgrade added now sits in the CREATE TABLE at the same position, so a fresh database gets the schema it had before. The upgrade fixture, its tests and the security-parameter open check are deleted with it, and the decision record now says the store starts fresh.

Delete unreferenced TypeScript exports

The 167 exports were referenced nowhere in the repository. Deleting them left further helpers, types and barrel lines with no remaining user, and those go too. Two fault-proof modules and one SDK module were left empty and are deleted. The eslint baseline drops the one localeCompare site that went with them.

Delete unreferenced Aiken library functions

Thirty-eight library functions and constants had no caller in any validator, library module or test. Removing them leaves every validator hash unchanged (1191 validators compared before and after) and the build warning count at its baseline.

Name three golden generators' Aiken outputs by full path

The preflight registry selects a golden check from the file paths its generator names. Once the JSON fixtures were gone, the staged-arm, serialise-loop and write-bits-loop generators only named their Aiken module as a bare file name joined to a directory, so an edit to the generated module no longer selected its own check. Name the module by its repository path, as the routing generator does. Also restore Prettier formatting of channels.json.

Delete the generated required-checks document

The 1,600-line document restated the preflight registry, and a CI step, a pre-push check and a channel existed only to keep the copy equal to the source. node scripts/preflight.mjs --list prints the checks a change selects, with their commands and capabilities, straight from the registry, so the docs that linked the document now point there. The misses-log rule moves into the registry's header comment, and build-guard enrollment is the one validator CI evidence can still reuse.

Delete unread and regenerable test fixtures

The resolver proof-fit sweep fixtures (the frozen sweep output, its unfit pin
and the pre-Option-B baseline) have had no reader since f69a0ddb2 deleted the
sweep test, and no generator exists to refresh them, so they guarded nothing.
They go, with the frozen channel, the skill's blind-spot note and the
test-quality audit section and ticket scope that described them.

The validation benchmark's ledger and transaction-sequence fixtures (about
35,000 lines) come from bench:fixtures:generate and nothing in CI reads them.
They are now gitignored; the benchmark's missing-fixture message names the
generate command, and the generator moves to the registry's ignored list.

tests/txs/txs_0.json held 1,000 one-to-one self-transfers, of which the CI
tests read only the first. It keeps that one; the codec and phase-A
benchmarks repeat it TX_LIMIT times instead of slicing the list.

Keep the TypeScript-compiler import ban to node runtime source

The ban landed on the block that covers all of midgard-node and midgard-node-tools, so it also refused the compiler in their tests and dev tooling, which may use it. It now sits on a src-only block. The shared import patterns are restated through one helper, which keeps the config under its 500-line cap; every other file resolves the same restrictions as before.

Delete unused benchmark, release and contributor helper scripts

Nothing in CI, production or the drill runs the benchmark regression check, the defect-signature tagger, the SDK tarball audit, the Dockerfile build-plan generator, the load watchdog, the nominal activity generator, the module-size inventory script, contrib reproduce, or the pstack dispatcher and work-log helpers. Their tests only exercised themselves. The Dockerfiles lose the generator's marker comments, and the docs and skills that pointed at the deleted commands now say what to do without them.

Write vector fixtures one vector per line

The remaining JSON vector fixtures and the script-budget table were written
with JSON.stringify(..., null, 2), which spreads every field of every vector
over its own indented line: about 62,000 lines for eleven files, and a diff
that shows a changed vector as scattered field lines.

golden-channel.mjs gains vectorsJson, which puts each top-level entry on its
own line and spreads an array or keyed object under it one compact element
per line. Every emitter of these files now writes through it, including
script-budgets.mjs for script-budgets.json; cek-builtin-step-evidence-vectors.json,
which is hand-maintained, was rewritten once the same way. Only the layout
changed: each file parses to the same value, in the same order, as before.

Delete the differential tests against the retired recursive walks

The CBOR codec, the semantic-Data encode, commit and rebuild, and the BLS expression evaluator were each rewritten as iterative walks, and these tests compared them against vendored copies of the recursive versions they replaced. The rewrites have landed; the copies now only pin the new code to the old code's behaviour, and the codec is also pinned by the cross-language golden channels.

The semantic-Data cases that need no oracle stay as plain tests in cek-proof-semantic.test.ts: a self-containing value is refused rather than overflowing the stack, a shared (DAG) value commits and rebuilds in linear time, a list with holes is refused, and a non-integer leaf is named.

Delete the repository drift scans and the mocked CLI wiring tests

The drift scans compare one file's text against another's (workflow steps against test files, shard counts against the matrix, doc entries against source names, package scripts against a flag list, env keys against a snapshot, removed provider names against node sources, HTTP tokens against the DA modules). They fail on edits that change no behaviour and are kept only by being re-derived. The CLI wiring tests mock their own package's modules and assert the calls between them. The owner ordered both kinds deleted.

Three behaviour tests in those files are kept: the acceptance CLI's deadline refusal stays in its file, the service-port refusals move to devnet-stack-service-ports.test.ts, and the journey catalogue keeps its fixture-selection tests while its literal owner counts go. The preflight registry no longer names the deleted self-tests, its own test drops the cases that named them, and the skills and the Node CI comment that pointed at them are corrected.
